key_terms.meaning: Porous solid such as activated carbon, silica gel or zeolite that holds solute molecules on its internal surface.
The solute or species removed from the fluid and held on the adsorbent surface.
q = qmax·K·C/(1 + K·C), where q is loading, C is fluid concentration, qmax is monolayer capacity and K is the adsorption constant.
q = K·C^(1/n), an empirical power-law fit where K and n are constants found from data.
Plot of exit concentration C/C0 against time or volume for a fixed bed; it rises when adsorbate first reaches the outlet.
The moving band inside a fixed bed where concentration falls from feed value to near zero.
Resin carrying fixed negative groups that swaps positive ions such as Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ for H⁺ or Na⁺.
Restoring resin capacity by washing with acid, caustic or brine so the held ions are replaced.
C − C* or C/C*, the amount by which concentration C exceeds equilibrium solubility C* at a given temperature.
Graph of saturation concentration C* against temperature for a given solute–solvent pair.
Birth of new crystal particles from a supersaturated solution, either spontaneously or on foreign surfaces.
Deposition of solute molecules onto existing crystal faces, increasing crystal size rather than number.
Mass of crystal product obtained per mass of solute fed, set by the solute balance and final solubility.
Heat released when solute leaves solution and joins the crystal lattice; it must be removed or supplied in the balance.
Mixed-suspension, mixed-product-removal crystallizer; a continuous stirred vessel with residence time τ = V/Q.
n = number of crystals per unit size interval per unit suspension volume, usually plotted as ln n against size L.
The spread of crystal sizes in a product, reported by number, length or mass and summarised by a dominant size.
Pressure-driven membrane process that pushes water through a dense membrane while rejecting dissolved salts.
Electric-field-driven process using ion-exchange membranes to move cations and anions out of a solution.
Low-pressure membrane process that retains macromolecules and colloids while passing water and small solutes.

takeaways: Adsorption capacity comes from surface area and pore structure, so adsorbent choice is as important as isotherm choice.
Langmuir and Freundlich equations turn equilibrium data into constants that can be used for batch and column calculations.
A fixed bed works until the mass-transfer zone reaches the exit; the breakthrough curve is the design record of that arrival.
Ion exchange is a reversible swapping of ions on a resin, and regeneration is part of every practical cycle.
Supersaturation is the driving force for crystallization; without it, neither nuclei nor crystal growth can occur.
Nucleation and growth compete for the same supersaturation, so the balance between them controls crystal number and size.
Crystallizer yield follows from a solute balance, while the heat balance fixes the cooling or evaporation duty.
The MSMPR model gives an exponential population-density plot whose slope and intercept yield growth and nucleation rates.
Membranes separate by pressure or electric driving force, and the choice among reverse osmosis, electrodialysis and ultrafiltration depends on the species to be removed.
bank_note: Long answers usually reward labelled diagrams, correct isotherm or population-density equations with every symbol defined, and a clear solute or heat balance worked step by step.

glossary.def: A porous solid that removes solute from a fluid by holding it on its surface.
The solute species that is adsorbed from the fluid onto the solid.
Accumulation of molecules at the surface of a solid or liquid rather than in its bulk.
Weak, reversible adsorption caused by van der Waals forces, with low heat release.
Strong adsorption involving chemical bonding, often irreversible and with high heat release.
A monolayer adsorption model written q = qmax·K·C/(1 + K·C).
An empirical adsorption model written q = K·C^(1/n).
A plot of outlet concentration against time or throughput for an adsorber or ion-exchange column.
The region in a fixed bed where the fluid concentration changes from feed value to nearly zero.
Reversible exchange of ions between a solution and a solid resin that keeps total charge balanced.
A resin that swaps positive ions from solution with positive ions held on its charged groups.
A chemical wash that restores the capacity of an adsorbent or ion-exchange resin.
The condition in which a solution contains more dissolved solute than its equilibrium solubility at that temperature.
A graph of saturation concentration against temperature for a solute in a solvent.
The formation of new crystal particles from a supersaturated solution.
The addition of solute to existing crystal faces so that crystals become larger.
The distribution of crystal sizes in a product, expressed by number, length or mass.
The number of crystals per unit size interval per unit volume of crystal suspension.
A continuous mixed-suspension, mixed-product-removal crystallizer modelled with residence time τ.
A pressure-driven membrane process that passes water while rejecting dissolved salts.
A pressure-driven membrane process that retains macromolecules and colloids while passing water and small solutes.
A membrane process that uses an electric field to move ions through ion-exchange membranes.
The fluid stream that passes through a membrane.
The fluid stream that is held back by a membrane and leaves more concentrated.
The flow rate of permeate per unit membrane area, usually in L/(m²·h) or m³/(m²·s).
